title: TE Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: Challenges concerning the October 3 and November 20, 2006 meetings were moot or addressed through nullification. The remaining complaint was denied, and Presbytery was affirmed regarding Lee’s stated-supply status, the expiration of his term, and appointment of the Judicial Commission.
first_summary: Lee challenged Presbytery’s treatment of his interim pastorate as stated supply, the expiration of his term, irregular meetings, and appointment of a Judicial Commission. The SJC found the meeting concerns moot, denied the remaining complaint, and affirmed Presbytery. It held that interim pastor meant stated supply under BCO 22-6, that the withdrawn renewal request left Lee’s one-year term expired, and that the Judicial Commission was properly constituted.
summary: Lee challenged irregular Presbytery meetings, classification of his interim pastorate as stated supply, expiration of his term, and appointment of a Judicial Commission. Meeting-related concerns were moot or resolved by nullification; the SJC otherwise denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. No pastoral call had been approved or installation conducted, and BCO 22-6 limited the stated-supply relationship to one year absent renewal. The ruling approved only the Commission’s appointment, not its later actions, which remained subject to pending complaints.

sources.supports: Judgments, moot meeting issues, denial, affirmance, and qualification concerning later commission actions.
Reasons for treating interim pastor as stated supply, finding the term expired, and approving the Judicial Commission’s composition.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The heading identifies consolidated Cases 2007-01, 2007-06, and 2007-07; section B separately identifies 2007-06 as Lee’s complaint and records the SJC’s judgment (lines 13, 119–125).
evidence_notes.dispute: Lee disputed meeting regularity, premature dissolution and stated-supply classification, and the Judicial Commission’s formation (lines 68–78).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Meeting concerns were moot or previously addressed; the complaint was otherwise denied and Presbytery affirmed because no pastoral call or installation existed, renewal was withdrawn, and the commission met BCO 15-2 composition requirements (lines 119–162).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC approved only appointment of the commissions, expressly withholding judgment on their later actions involved in pending complaints (lines 108–109).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No external decision was incorporated by reference.

source_limits: The source presents a consolidated opinion; the synopsis isolates the judgment and reasoning expressly assigned to Case 2007-06.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged meetings, pastoral classification and expiration, and commission appointment.
score_reasons.decision: Preserves moot meeting issues, denial, affirmance, and the limited scope of the commission ruling.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: States the absence of a pastoral call or installation, BCO 22-6’s annual limit, withdrawal of renewal, and proper commission composition.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Highlights the distinction between an interim pastor/stated supply and an installed pastor, plus the appointment-versus-actions limitation.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates Case 2007-06 from the consolidated cases and distinguishes adopted holdings from Lee’s arguments.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the mixed outcome and qualification.
